cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Northern District of California
cases.FraudEntity: Simon Katz; Veronica Katz (former CEO of HealthNow Home Healthcare); Vennesa Herrera (former employee); Pharadja Andrews (former employee); HealthNow Home Healthcare (home health agency)
cases.SchemeSummary: HealthNow Home Healthcare used unqualified medical professionals to perform home health patient assessments outside their scope of practice, billed Medicare for services never provided, and altered medical records/forged physician signatures, plus submitted falsified documents to California Department of Public Health inspectors to keep Medicare billing privileges; the agency collected over $3 million and Simon Katz took $300,000, and he instructed an employee to lie to the FBI. Figures span co-defendants: Veronica Katz was sentenced to 24 months, $543,634.34 restitution and a $50,000 fine, while Simon Katz awaits sentencing after jury conviction.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Kentucky
cases.FraudEntity: Delores Jordan (owner of Serenity Keeper's, LLC); Ernest Williams (operator of sober homes); Serenity Keeper's, LLC (sober home company); Jerome Davis (co-defendant, owner of X-Tremly for Christ, LLC); Dashawn Dawkins (co-defendant); Lily Bell (kickback payer)
cases.SchemeSummary: Jordan, owner of a Fayette County sober home company, solicited and received kickbacks (checks, cash, ACH, and $5,000 'consulting' payments to co-defendant Davis's company) in exchange for referring residents' urine drug tests to three labs, causing Medicaid and Medicare to pay those labs about $2,569,946 for tests that were not ordered or reviewed by a medical provider. Serenity Keepers also billed Medicaid for six hours per day of peer support services that were not provided and were not delivered by licensed peer support specialists, with Williams receiving $365,374.72 as a percentage of amounts billed; Jordan got 60 months, Williams five years' probation, and Davis 12 months and a day.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
cases.FraudEntity: Camille S. Childress (operator/owner of Inspiring Angels LLC); Inspiring Angels LLC
cases.SchemeSummary: Childress enrolled her home health company Inspiring Angels LLC in Missouri Medicaid using paperwork falsely naming another person as owner to conceal her ownership and a 2012 conviction, then billed Medicaid for in-home services never rendered, including for clients who were hospitalized and for visits with no timesheets or documentation, collecting at least $174,496 in 2021-2022. A related release notes she was later sentenced to 15 months and ordered to repay $174,496.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
cases.FraudEntity: Camille S. Childress (operator/owner of Inspiring Angels LLC); Inspiring Angels LLC (home health care company)
cases.SchemeSummary: Childress enrolled her home health company with Missouri Medicaid using paperwork falsely naming another person as owner to hide her disqualifying 2012 conviction, then billed Missouri Medicaid $174,496 for home health services never provided, including for clients who were hospitalized and for visits with no timesheets or documentation.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
cases.FraudEntity: Natavia Boyd-Wells (owner of Touch of the Heart Home Health Care LLC); Touch of the Heart Home Health Care LLC
cases.PayerName: Missouri Medicaid Program; U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Community Care Network
cases.SchemeSummary: Owner of a home health company submitted hundreds of claims to Missouri Medicaid and the VA Community Care Network for home healthcare services never provided, including on dates when veteran patients were hospitalized, and fabricated documentation in response to a Medicaid audit request; losses were at least $109,751 to Medicaid and $100,563 to the VA.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan; Justice Department Criminal Division, Fraud Section / National Fraud Enforcement Division
cases.FraudEntity: Ruby Scott (nurse, owner of Delta Home Health Care LLC); Delta Home Health Care LLC
cases.State_County: Michigan - Oakland County (Farmington Hills); Michigan - Wayne County (Detroit)
cases.SchemeSummary: Scott bribed a Detroit hospital discharge nurse (over $130,000, roughly $100-$300 per patient via CashApp, PayPal, check and cash) to fax confidential Medicare patient records to her home health agency, then billed Medicare for home health services using those stolen patient profiles, falsely representing that physicians had certified the patients as homebound and eligible when no doctor had evaluated them; some patients never received services and files were missing for over a third of billed patients, causing about $1.6 million in Medicare losses.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Pennsylvania
cases.FraudEntity: Blessings 4 Ever Home Care Agency LLC (in-home care provider); V&V Management Solutions LLC (related management company)
cases.SchemeSummary: Home care agency allegedly fabricated or backdated 181 training certificates and personnel documents so personal care attendants appeared to meet state/Medicaid training requirements, then billed Pennsylvania Medicaid for their services (Jan 2015-Dec 2018); it also billed 1,141 claims for in-home personal care for 209 beneficiaries on days those beneficiaries were hospital inpatients all day (June 2020-Dec 2023). Resolved for $1 million in a qui tam action, with the relator receiving 21% of the federal recovery.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Kris Agency & Home Care, Inc. (Queens home care agency); Career Development Center of Queens, Inc. (home health aide training center)
cases.SchemeSummary: A Queens home care agency and an affiliated home health aide training center applied for two pandemic-era second-draw PPP loans, falsely certifying that they and their affiliates had fewer than 300 employees and failing to disclose their affiliation with each other, thereby obtaining over $1.8 million in loans and subsequent loan forgiveness; resolved via a $2,347,133.10 False Claims Act qui tam settlement.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri
cases.FraudEntity: Daniell Green (owner and operator of A&L Angels Home Healthcare Services LLC); Dejuan Bingham; Kimberly Diazascencio; Thomas Keith; A&L Angels Home Healthcare Services LLC
cases.SchemeSummary: Owner of a Bridgeton home health company and her associates allegedly created false timesheets showing home health services never provided, including on dates patients were hospitalized or when listed workers were employed elsewhere, and recruited Medicaid patients to lend their names to fraudulent claims; Green also allegedly submitted a false Medicaid participation agreement claiming providers were in the Family Care Safety Registry and background-checked, concealing Bingham's felony conviction. Proceeds funded vacations, furniture and luxury goods.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division and U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Oklahoma
cases.SchemeSummary: Traditions self-disclosed that its McAlester, Oklahoma location billed Medicare for home health services that were not medically necessary (2021-2024), and that from 2019-2024 it paid remuneration to physician-medical directors in Oklahoma and Texas who referred Medicare beneficiaries for home health services, implicating the Anti-Kickback Statute and Stark Law.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Florida
cases.FraudEntity: Medical Services of America, Inc.; Traditional Home Care, Inc. d/b/a Community Home Health Services (home health providers)
cases.SchemeSummary: Community Home Health Services allegedly paid bonuses to an employee based on the volume of Medicare patient referrals made by the employee's physician spouse, then furnished and billed Medicare for those designated home health services in violation of the Stark Law; resolved for $702,541.20 including $379,752 restitution following a qui tam suit.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of New York
cases.FraudEntity: Elaine Antao (marketer/recruiter); Manal Wasef (marketer/recruiter); Amran Hashmi; Joseph Helmy; Amal Ismail; Zakia Khan; Seema Memon
cases.SchemeSummary: Antao and Wasef acted as marketers/recruiters for two Brooklyn social adult day care centers and a home health fiscal intermediary, referring Medicaid recipients in exchange for kickbacks and paying cash bribes to beneficiaries; over $68 million was billed to Medicaid for adult day care and home health services that were not provided or were induced by kickbacks, with proceeds laundered through multiple business entities to generate the bribe cash. Seven defendants have pleaded guilty; the two agreed to forfeit approximately $1 million collectively.

cases.JurisdictionName: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of West Virginia
cases.FraudEntity: Raymond C. "Rocky" Meadows II (founder and director, Lifehouse Inc.); Helen Crutcher Meadows (collector supervisor, Lifehouse Inc.); West Virginia Sleep Centers, LLC (sleep laboratory, civil settlement)
cases.State_County: West Virginia - Cabell County (Huntington); West Virginia - Raleigh County (Beckley)
cases.PayerName: Medicaid (West Virginia); Veterans Administration Community Health program
cases.SchemeSummary: Criminal complaints allege the Meadowses, who ran the Lifehouse Inc. sober living/recovery program, falsified and submitted timesheets to a drug testing laboratory for drug testing work never performed - including 32 hours of weekly overtime for months and hours billed while on out-of-state vacations - and the lab paid them and then obtained reimbursement from federal and state health care programs. Separately, West Virginia Sleep Centers LLC paid $120,000 to settle allegations it billed Medicaid and the VA Community Health program for sleep studies and polysomnogram reports prepared and signed by unqualified non-physician staff from January 2016 through January 2020.
